review_notes:
I read the whole file. It has no @[simp] attributes, no simp sets and no simp-normal-form lemmas. The declarations are bounds, measurability facts, integral-splitting lemmas and one large existence proof. Their statements are proof-oriented, with explicit hypotheses and conditional `if` indicators. Examples are `norm_annulus_condition_iff`, `integral_split_five` and `singular_tAnnLin_cancel`.

I found no competing rules, rewrite cycles, unwanted expansion or missing canonical simp lemma that the file's own uses would justify. Tagging the iff and cancellation lemmas with `@[simp]` would be speculative. They carry side conditions such as `0 < ‖L‖`, and their right-hand sides introduce divisions. The file also uses them only through explicit `rw` or `have`. The `simp_all` and `simp only` calls inside proofs are local proof choices, not part of the simp interface.

I did not run Lean, so I did not test any simp behaviour. I also did not search other files for downstream simp uses of these lemmas.
